## What I measured

`worktree()` copies the repo so a test can edit `src/` and run the real correspondence gate. The tree is 7.3 GB, and the plan claimed the copy was dragging generated directories through every call and could distort the pytest-xdist benchmark.

```
before   0.40s   63.9 MB   1594 files
after    0.03s    6.7 MB    198 files
```

**63.9 MB reached the copy, not 7.3 GB.** `.venv` was already in `IGNORE` and `shutil.ignore_patterns` applies at every level of the walk, so the nested virtualenvs under `technology-universe/runtimes/` — nearly all of the 7 GB — were never copied.

## The plan's rationale was wrong, and this corrects it

**This has no effect in CI.** A fresh checkout is 194 tracked files. `node_modules/` exists only where `npm ci` runs — the e2e workflow — and correspondence runs in `verify.yml`. `htmlcov/`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`, `.claude/` are all absent there too.

In CI the copy was *already* the 198-file case. It cannot protect a GitHub benchmark from copy noise, because there is none there to protect it from.

What it actually is: 3 call sites, ~1.1s of local test time, and a copy that no longer varies with whatever a developer happened to build.

## Safe because the gate declares its inputs

`correspondence_gate.py:92-94`:

```python
SRC    = Path("src")
SPECS  = Path("semantics/specs")
PROOFS = Path("semantics/proofs")
```

Every added path is verifiably outside that set, held there by two tests:

- **structural** — reads the gate's source, fails if it ever mentions an excluded directory
- **behavioural** — plants all four directories in one copy, omits them from another, runs the real gate over both, asserts exit code and output agree

`technology-universe` is **not** excluded — it is tracked content (64 files), and excluding tracked content is the one change that could alter what the gate sees.

## Two defects in my own test, found by running it

The behavioural comparison first asserted raw stdout equality (fails on the report timestamp), then still failed on `[DURATION] 6049ms` vs `5826ms`. Comparing raw stdout asserts both runs started at the same instant and took the same milliseconds. Both normalised, with the reason recorded so nobody deletes it as noise.

full suite exit 0 · `test_correspondence` 58 passed · pyright 0 · gate_integrity 0 · security_gate 0 · `git diff --check` clean

**TCB:** none. `tests/` only. No gate, workflow, manifest, threshold or required context changes.
